# notame - Workflow for non-targeted LC-MS metabolic profiling ![](reference/figures/notame_logo.png)

The notame packages can be used to analyze preprocessed LC-MS data in
non-targeted metabolomics. Notame was developed at the [research group
of nutritional metabolomics at University of Eastern
Finland](https://hanhinevalab.com/home) and [Afekta
Technologies](https://afekta.com/), a spinoff metabolomics company. We
use notame as a way to bundle together all the preprocessing methods we
use for our non-targeted LC-MS metabolomics data, so it mainly consists
of methods found in other packages, and a bunch of visualizations we
have found useful.

For more detailed information on how we run our LC-MS experiments and
where this package fits in our workflow, you can find the paper here:
[“notame”: Workflow for Non-Targeted LC-MS Metabolic
Profiling](https://www.mdpi.com/2218-1989/10/4/135). A huge thank you
for everyone involved in the paper!

Currently, notame is developed by Afekta Technologies and was reworked
for Bioconductor to promote interoperability with functionality that can
complement the notame workflow. This resulted in some breaking changes
(see NEWS for user-facing changes). See the vignettes and documentation
for more information, for example on the
[website](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/).

### What does notame do?

Before we go into the list of features, it is good for you to know how
the workflow in our lab works. The first step is to take raw data files
created by the LC-MS instrument and create a peak table using a peak
picking software (we use
[MS-DIAL](https://systemsomicslab.github.io/compms/msdial/main.html)).
After peak picking with the dedicated software, we use R for data
preprocessing, quality control, statistical analysis and visualization.
We then use the obtained results in identification of the actual
metabolites. During the years, we ended up with various scripts that
were hard to handle and update, so we decided to make notame to keep
things under control.

Here is a list of the current main functionalities of notame:

- Reading data from Excel spreadsheets created with MS-DIAL
- Data is stored in a SummarizedExperiment object that holds all the
  information about the features and samples along with the feature
  abundance matrix. This allows for a simple interface for all of the
  functions in notame, as there is no need to juggle with different
  matrices/data frames.
- Drift correction: correcting for systematic drift in the intensity of
  molecular features using cubic spline correction (see [Kirwan &
  Broadhurst et al.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00216-013-6856-7))
- Identifying and flagging (or removing) low-quality molecular features
  using quality metrics defined by [Broadhurst et
  al.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11306-018-1367-3)
- Imputing missing values, multiple strategies available. Random forest
  imputation recommended, see [Kokla et
  al.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-019-3110-0)
- Batch effect correction: correcting for systematic variation between
  batches
- A novel method for clustering similar molecular features
- A bunch of statistical analyses, both feature-wise tests and
  multivariate models
- A rather nice set of visualizations for use in quality control,
  explorative analysis and interpretation of results from statistical
  tests

## Installation and getting started

### Bioc-release

    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
        install.packages("BiocManager")

    BiocManager::install("notame")

### Bioc-devel

    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
        install.packages("BiocManager")

    # The following initializes usage of Bioc devel
    BiocManager::install(version='devel')

    BiocManager::install("notame")

## Credits and license

The first version of notame was written by Anton Klåvus for his master’s
thesis in Bioinformatics at Aalto university (published under former
name Anton Mattsson), while working for University of Eastern Finland
and Afekta Technologies. Notame is inspired by analysis scripts written
by Jussi Paananen, Oskari Timonen and Anton Klåvus at University of
Eastern Finland. The algorithm for clustering molecular features
originating from the same compound is based on MATLAB code written by
David Broadhurst. Development was picked up by Atte Lihtamo, Retu
Haikonen, Vilhelm Suksi and Leo Lahti, leading to the Bioconductor
release.

If you find any bugs or other things to fix, please submit an issue on
GitHub! All contributions to notame are always welcome!

notame is published under an MIT license (tl;dr: it’s really
permissive!)

# Package index

## Tabular data preprocessing

- [`mark_nas()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/mark_nas.md)
  : Mark specified values as missing
- [`flag_detection()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag_detection.md)
  : Flag features with low detection rate
- [`flag_contaminants()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag_contaminants.md)
  : Flag contaminants based on blanks
- [`correct_drift()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/correct_drift.md)
  : Correct drift using cubic spline
- [`ruvs_qc()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/ruvs_qc.md)
  : Remove Unwanted Variation (RUV) between batches
- [`pca_bhattacharyya_dist()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/pca_bhattacharyya_dist.md)
  : Bhattacharyya distance between batches in PCA space
- [`perform_repeatability()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/perform_repeatability.md)
  : Compute repeatability measures
- [`assess_quality()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/assess_quality.md)
  : Assess quality information of features
- [`quality()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/quality.md)
  : Extract quality information of features
- [`flag_quality`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag_quality.md)
  [`flag_quality()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag_quality.md)
  : Flag low-quality features
- [`flag_report()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag_report.md)
  : A report of flagged features
- [`impute_rf()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/impute_rf.md)
  : Impute missing values using random forest
- [`impute_simple()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/impute_simple.md)
  : Simple imputation
- [`cluster_features()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/cluster_features.md)
  : Cluster correlated features originating from the same metabolite
- [`compress_clusters()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/compress_clusters.md)
  : Compress clusters of features to a single feature
- [`pqn_normalization()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/pqn_normalization.md)
  : Probabilistic quotient normalization
- [`inverse_normalize()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/inverse_normalize.md)
  : Inverse-rank normalization

  : Sample dendrogram (from notameViz)
- [`plot_sample_heatmap()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/plot_sample_heatmap.html)
  : Sample heatmap (from notameViz)
- [`plot_pca_loadings()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/plot_pca_loadings.html)
  : PCA loadings plot (from notameViz)
- [`plot_quality()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/plot_quality.html)
  : Plot quality metrics (from notameViz)
- [`save_batch_plots()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/save_batch_plots.html)
  : Save batch correction plots (from notameViz)
- [`save_dc_plots()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/save_dc_plots.html)
  : Save drift correction plots (from notameViz)
- [`visualize_clusters()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameViz/man/visualize_clusters.html)
  : Visualize clusters of features (from notameViz)

## Feature selection

### Univariate analysis

- [`perform_lm()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_lm.html)
  : Linear models (from notameStats)
- [`perform_logistic()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_logistic.html)
  : Logistic regression (from notameStats)
- [`perform_lmer()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_lmer.html)
  : Linear mixed models (from notameStats)
- [`perform_oneway_anova()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_oneway_anova.html)
  : Welch's ANOVA and classic ANOVA (from notameStats)
- [`perform_lm_anova()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_lm_anova.html)
  : Linear models ANOVA table (from notameStats)
- [`perform_t_test()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_t_test.html)
  : Pairwise and paired t-tests (from notameStats)
- [`perform_kruskal_wallis()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_kruskal_wallis.html)
  : Kruskal-Wallis rank-sum test (from notameStats)
- [`perform_non_parametric()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_non_parametric.html)
  : Pairwise and paired non-parametric tests (from notameStats)
- [`perform_correlation_tests()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_correlation_tests.html)
  : Correlation test (from notameStats)
- [`perform_auc()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_auc.html)
  : Area under curve (from notameStats)
- [`perform_homoscedasticity_tests()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/perform_homoscedasticity_tests.html)
  : Test homoscedasticity (from notameStats)
- [`cohens_d()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/cohens_d.html) :
  Cohen's D (from notameStats)
- [`fold_change()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/fold_change.html)
  : Fold change (from notameStats)
- [`summary_statistics()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/summary_statistics.html)
  : Summary statistics (from notameStats)
- [`summarize_results()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/notameStats/man/summarize_results.html)
  : Statistics cleaning (from notameStats)

## Object utilities

- [`import_from_excel()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/import_from_excel.md)
  : Read formatted Excel files
- [`import_from_msdial()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/import_from_msdial.md)
  : Import data from a TSV file created by MS-DIAL
- [`write_to_excel()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/write_to_excel.md)
  : Write results to Excel file
- [`flag()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag.md)
  [`` `flag<-`() ``](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/flag.md)
  : Get and set the values in the flag column
- [`drop_flagged()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/drop_flagged.md)
  : Drop flagged features
- [`drop_qcs()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/drop_qcs.md)
  : Drop QC samples
- [`join_rowData()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/join_rowData.md)
  : Join new columns to feature data
- [`join_colData()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/join_colData.md)
  : Join new columns to pheno data
- [`combined_data()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/combined_data.md)
  : Retrieve both sample information and features
- [`merge_notame_sets()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/merge_notame_sets.md)
  : Merge SummarizedExperiment objects together
- [`fix_object()`](https://hanhineva-lab.github.io/notame/reference/fix_object.md)
  : Fix object for functioning of notame
